title: Find Overlapping Shifts II
statement:
One table records work shifts:

- `EmployeeShifts(employee_id, start_time, end_time)`: one row per shift; `(employee_id, start_time)` is unique and every shift ends strictly after it starts. Times are `DATETIME` values on whole minutes, and a shift may run past midnight.

Two shifts overlap when they belong to the **same employee**, start on the **same date** (the date part of `start_time`; a shift that runs past midnight still belongs to the day it began), and each one starts before the other ends. Shifts that only touch (one ends exactly when the other begins) do not overlap, and shifts starting on different dates never overlap, even when their hours intersect.

For every employee in the table, report:

- `employee_id`.
- `max_overlapping_shifts`: the largest number of that employee's shifts that overlap all at once, that is, shifts with the same start date that are all in progress at one moment. A shift is in progress from its `start_time` up to, but not including, its `end_time`, so the value is at least 1.
- `total_overlap_duration`: for every pair of overlapping shifts, the minutes the two have in common, summed over all such pairs (`0` when nothing overlaps).

Order the rows by `employee_id` ascending.
constraints: times are whole minutes written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
reference:
WITH pairs AS (
  SELECT a.employee_id,
    TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, b.start_time, LEAST(a.end_time, b.end_time)) AS overlap_minutes
  FROM EmployeeShifts AS a
  JOIN EmployeeShifts AS b
    ON b.employee_id = a.employee_id
    AND DATE(b.start_time) = DATE(a.start_time)
    AND b.start_time > a.start_time
    AND b.start_time < a.end_time
),
concurrent AS (
  SELECT s.employee_id, s.start_time, COUNT(*) AS active_shifts
  FROM EmployeeShifts AS s
  JOIN EmployeeShifts AS o
    ON o.employee_id = s.employee_id
    AND DATE(o.start_time) = DATE(s.start_time)
    AND o.start_time <= s.start_time
    AND o.end_time > s.start_time
  GROUP BY s.employee_id, s.start_time
),
peaks AS (
  SELECT employee_id, MAX(active_shifts) AS max_overlapping_shifts
  FROM concurrent
  GROUP BY employee_id
)
SELECT pk.employee_id,
  pk.max_overlapping_shifts,
  IFNULL(SUM(pr.overlap_minutes), 0) AS total_overlap_duration
FROM peaks AS pk
LEFT JOIN pairs AS pr
  ON pr.employee_id = pk.employee_id
GROUP BY pk.employee_id, pk.max_overlapping_shifts
ORDER BY pk.employee_id;
brute:
WITH events AS (
  SELECT employee_id, DATE(start_time) AS shift_date, start_time AS moment, 1 AS delta FROM EmployeeShifts
  UNION ALL
  SELECT employee_id, DATE(start_time), end_time, -1 FROM EmployeeShifts
),
sweep AS (
  SELECT employee_id,
    SUM(delta) OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id, shift_date ORDER BY moment, delta ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running
  FROM events
)
SELECT w.employee_id,
  MAX(w.running) AS max_overlapping_shifts,
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(GREATEST(0, TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, GREATEST(x.start_time, y.start_time), LEAST(x.end_time, y.end_time)))), 0) / 2
   FROM EmployeeShifts AS x, EmployeeShifts AS y
   WHERE x.employee_id = w.employee_id AND y.employee_id = w.employee_id AND x.start_time <> y.start_time
     AND DATE(x.start_time) = DATE(y.start_time)) AS total_overlap_duration
FROM sweep AS w
GROUP BY w.employee_id
ORDER BY w.employee_id
notes:
## Intuition

Both numbers come from comparing an employee's shifts with each other, which is a **self-join** of `EmployeeShifts` on `employee_id`, restricted to shifts with the same start date (`DATE(start_time)`).

- The shared time of two overlapping shifts runs from the later start to the earlier end. Pairing each shift only with same-day shifts that start later (and before it ends) lists every overlapping pair exactly once.
- The number of shifts in progress only goes up when a shift starts, so the peak is reached at some shift's start. Counting, at each start, the same-day shifts that have begun and not yet ended gives every candidate peak.

## Approach

1. `pairs`: join shift `a` to every shift `b` of the same employee and start date with `a.start_time < b.start_time < a.end_time`; the overlap is `TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, b.start_time, LEAST(a.end_time, b.end_time))`.
2. `concurrent`: for each shift `s`, count the shifts `o` of the same employee and start date with `o.start_time <= s.start_time < o.end_time` (this includes `s` itself).
3. `peaks`: the largest such count per employee.
4. Final select: left-join `peaks` to `pairs`, sum the minutes (`IFNULL` turns "no pairs" into 0) and order by `employee_id`.

## Example 1, step by step

Every shift starts on 2023-10-01 (the last one ends at midnight but still belongs to that day), so the date test removes nothing.

- `pairs`: employee 1 gives 120 (09:00 and 15:00 shifts share 15:00-17:00), 60 (09:00 and 16:00 share 16:00-17:00) and 420 (15:00 and 16:00 share 16:00-23:00); employee 2 gives 360 (11:00-17:00). Employee 3 has no pair.
- `concurrent`: employee 1 has 1, 2, 3 shifts in progress at 09:00, 15:00, 16:00; employee 2 has 1, 2; employee 3 has 1.
- `peaks`: 3, 2 and 1.
- Result: `(1, 3, 600)`, `(2, 2, 360)`, `(3, 1, 0)`.

## Complexity

- Time: each self-join compares a shift with the other shifts of the same employee, about O(n · k) for n shifts and at most k shifts per employee (O(n²) in the worst case).
- Space: O(n + p) for the per-shift counts and the p overlapping pairs.

## Pitfalls

- The shared part ends at the **earlier** end: `a.end_time - b.start_time` is wrong when `b` lies inside `a`. Keep the comparisons strict, since touching shifts (08:00-12:00 and 12:00-16:00) never run together.
- Shifts starting on different dates never overlap: a shift from 02:00 on 2023-10-02 shares nothing with one that began at 23:00 the day before, even though their hours intersect (Test 6).
- Counting overlapping pairs is not the peak: three shifts chained 08-12, 11-15, 14-18 have two overlapping pairs but never more than 2 at once.
- An inner join to `pairs` drops employees without any overlap; they must still appear with 0.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pairs` | one row per overlapping pair of an employee's same-day shifts, with its shared minutes |
| `a`, `b` | the earlier-starting and later-starting shift of a pair |
| `concurrent` | for each shift start, how many shifts of that day are in progress then |
| `s`, `o` | the shift whose start is examined, and a same-day shift that may cover it |
| `peaks` | each employee's `max_overlapping_shifts` |
| `pk`, `pr` | `peaks` and `pairs` in the final left join |

narration.1: The first stage lists every overlapping pair of shifts belonging to one employee.
narration.3: Two shifts share time from the later start (b) to whichever shift ends first.
narration.5: A self-join pairs each shift with the other shifts of the same employee.
narration.7: Only shifts that start on the same date can overlap.
narration.8: Requiring b to start after a lists each pair once, with a as the earlier shift.
narration.9: b must also start before a ends; touching shifts are not paired.
narration.11: The second stage measures how many shifts are running at each shift start.
narration.16: Only shifts that started on the same date as s are counted.
narration.17: Shift o is in progress at s.start_time if it has started by then...
narration.18: ...and has not yet ended, so a shift ending exactly then is not counted.
narration.22: The peak for each employee is the largest of those counts.
narration.28: Summing the pair overlaps gives the total; IFNULL turns an employee with no pairs into 0.
narration.30: A left join keeps employees whose shifts never overlap.
narration.33: Rows come out by employee_id, as required.
